title.narrative: A Partnership for Inclusive Prosperity / Paseria Ba Prosperidade Inkluzivu (PROSIVU)

description.narrative: A Partnership for Inclusive Prosperity / Paseria Ba Prosperidade Inkluzivu (PROSIVU) is Australia's main program for providing governance and economic development support to Timor-Leste's central government agencies and economic line-ministries. PROSIVU works with Australia's other bilateral investments, including on targeting blockages to service delivery, and working with Government counterparts, civil society and the private sector on priority economic reforms to grow and diversify the economy.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Following Timor-Leste’s successful accession to WTO, PROSIVU has played a central role in supporting Timor-Leste’s WTO post-accession phase, with a strong focus on fulfilling outstanding post-accession priorities, and legal reform. WTO membership provides a framework for economic diversification, integration into global markets, and domestic reforms to attract investment and improve governance in Timor-Leste, complementary to the ASEAN accession process. PROSIVU supported the Office of the Minister Coordinator for Economic Affairs (MCAE) to develop the Timor-Leste Post-Accession Vision and Strategy 2024–2031, outlining priority actions for implementing WTO commitments and led socialisation efforts, delivering outreach sessions with civil society, media, and public institutions to raise awareness of WTO obligations. ‍ In coordination with relevant agencies, PROSIVU has provided regular updates to the Interministerial Commission on WTO commitments progress and key issues. PROSIVU has also played a critical role in supporting government participation in international trade forums, such as the Ministerial Roundtable on Investment in Tourism: Catalysing Change in Abu Dhabi. Furthermore, the program supported the drafting of the Competition Law in close coordination with UNCTAD and prepared key documentation for its presentation to the Council of Ministers and the National Parliament.

In 2023-2024, PROSIVU significantly advanced Timor-Leste's ASEAN accession. Key achievements include: (1) supported the drafting a National Implementation Plan (NIP) for ASEAN accession, developing monitoring systems, and establishing mechanisms for effective inter-ministerial coordination; (2) completed reviews of 65 ASEAN core legal instruments and statistical requirements, identified Timor-Leste’s policy and legislative gaps in meeting such commitments; (3) completed reviews of Timor-Leste’s key laws including the Customs Code, Private Investment Law and Rules of Origin Regime, for amendments and development of new subsidiary legislation; (4) successfully designed and supported three whole-of-Government interministerial consultation meetings; and 12 technical door-to-door consultations with key ministries, presenting the identified gaps and proposed next steps; (5) supported high-level briefings and participation in ASEAN summit and ministerial meetings; (6) successfully organized a training workshop on ASEAN Trade and Investment Negotiations for more than 100 key officials.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: In 2024, PROSIVU made substantial contributions to Timor-Leste’s preparation for the introduction of a Value Added Tax (VAT) system, a key requirement for ASEAN accession and strengthening existing government revenue collection mechanisms. The program supported the development of an economic analysis that informed the VAT Policy Paper, and the VAT Steering Committee, which then endorsed the VAT Implementation Roadmap. To strengthen institutional capacity, the program facilitated a basic VAT course for 42 officials—64% of whom were women—with 25 participants successfully completing the course and receiving certificates from the Minister of Finance. ‍ PROSIVU also provided drafting support for the Terms of Reference for IT readiness and VAT business process mapping, both critical for building the necessary digital infrastructure. ‍ In 2025, the program assisted in refining the draft VAT Law prepared by the Ministry of Finance’s legal adviser, coordinated stakeholder engagement with the National Chamber of Commerce, and developed a VAT sensitization plan. PROSIVU also supported a structural review of the Tax Authority to ensure its readiness for VAT implementation. To strengthen outreach, the program contributed to the VAT communications strategy and secured a partnership with the Chamber of Commerce to enhance engagement with the business community.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: PROSIVU collaborated with the Government of Timor-Leste to conduct key labour surveys through the Secretariat of State for Professional Training and Employment (SEFOPE). Notable surveys include the Well-being of Returned Migrant Workers, Tracer Studies of TVET Graduates, the Enterprise & Skills Survey 2023, and the Labour Market Outlook 2023. Recent reports, shared with stakeholders and available online, influence key policy decisions. The Well-being survey fosters collaboration between SEFOPE, United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), National Institute of Statistics of Timor-Leste (INE-TL), Flinders University and others to improve reintegration programmes. The tracer studies led SEFOPE to increase the 2024 TVET budget, facilitating the establishment of new Training Centres. SEFOPE advocates for increased national internship participation across sectors and plans TVET sector enhancements together with the National Institute for Manpower Development (INDMO) and Australian Pacific Training Coalition.

PROSIVU supported the Ministry of Finance with the 2025 and 2026 State Budgets by developing the budget calendar and preparing training and briefing materials on planning, program budgeting, and budget cycle management. Further assistance was provided to review draft Annual Action Plans (AAPs) from line ministries and support the development of budget documents, including the Budget Report Book, AAP A and B, Budget Marker, and the Citizens Budget. This has improved transparency and enhanced the usability of budget information, to support decentralization with more effective planning and decision-making at the subnational level. ‍ This has resulted in major improvements to the quality of municipal budget reporting. In previous years, the Development State Budget Book – Report presented municipal allocations without providing deeper analysis. In 2025, a new section titled "Decentralization and Local Development: Investment in Municipalities" was added providing a comprehensive and analytical overview of municipal budgets, featuring: ‍ •Detailed analysis of municipal allocations. ‍ •New tables showing allocations by program and by municipality. ‍ •Information on school grants and the School Feeding Program. ‍ •Allocations for the National Program for Village Development and Integrated Municipal Development Planning. ‍ •Budget allocations for sucos (villages). ‍ •Per capita budget allocations by municipality.

PROSIVU, through its advisory support (5 advisers) to national secretariats and line agencies, has played a key role in supporting the Timor-Leste Government to successfully navigate the WTO accession process, which began in November 2016 and concluded with successful negotiations in January 2024. PROSIVU supported a WTO accession socialisation program at the municipal level, provided technical assistance to develop a Trade Policy Statement and consolidate post-accession documents, and supported successful bilateral negotiations. The WTO accession protocol was ratified by the Timor-Leste National Parliament on 3 June 2024, and Timor-Leste will officially become a WTO Member on 30 August 2024. WTO accession is pivotal for Timor-Leste's growth and prosperity. It provides a transparent, rules-based framework for Timor-Leste’s international trade, market access, and sustainable economic development goals. PROSIVU will continue to support Timor-Leste to implement its WTO obligations.

The Australian-funded PROSIVU programme provided technical assistance to support the development, implementation and monitoring of the Maubisse Declaration Phase III, which holds the Government of Timor-Leste accountable for strengthening rural women's economic empowerment. This included facilitating the development of indicators and a monitoring system based on insights from previous analyses that were then validated through a workshop with key stakeholders. This monitoring system enables accurate tracking of progress and achievements, and will also support the identification of areas for improvement throughout implementation. In addition, through PROSIVU‘s advocacy and awareness efforts, SSE was able to secure $15,000 (AUD22,500) in the 2024 General State Budget for the implementation of key activities under the Declaration."

Through Australian support, the Government of Timor-Leste developed and endorsed a new Medium-Term Planning Framework. The Framework enables planning that bridges the gap between the long-term Strategic Development Plan and annual plans, and provides guidance for short-term plans, such as annual budgets, to ensure the government’s proposed resource allocation is priority-based and likely to achieve the Government’s intended objectives. So far, Australia has supported the development of Medium-Term Plans for 4 key sectors, including Education and Training, Public Works, Agriculture, and Health, with more sector plans currently being developed.

Through PROSIVU, Australia is supporting Timor-Leste’s accession as the 11th member state of ASEAN. PROSIVU’s imbedded advisors provide capacity building and technical assistance to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation (MNEC), to meet requirements of ASEAN Accession and enhance its participation in the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) and broader regional frameworks. ‍ Examples of support provided to MNEC include: ‍ • inputs to statements for the Minister and Vice Minister at the 57th ASEAN Foreign Ministers Meeting in Lao PDR ‍ •inputs for the Senior Economics Officials' meeting statement at the ASEAN Economic Ministers Meeting ‍ •prepared the Director General for ASEAN Accession’s briefing for the Malaysian Ambassador on AEC legal instruments ‍ •prepared a revenue loss analysis for ATIGA tariff commitments ‍ •prepared a presentation on AEC accession, addressing political, economic, and technical aspects aimed at raising awareness among government stakeholders at both national and municipal levels ‍ •supported high-level briefings for bilateral meetings, including with Malaysia’s PM and at Singapore’s Business Forum ‍ •reviewed the MoU with the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia ‍ •updated the Legislative Action Plan referencing WTO commitments ‍ •inputs for the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement compliance assessments.

description.narrative: Timor-Leste’s aspirations around ASEAN membership will be integral to its economic diversification and resilience efforts. Through Australian support, a package was designed to assist Timor-Leste’s ASEAN accession process. Some key activities included embedding technical advisors into ministries, including MNEC, developing trade statistics and standards, launching a trade facilitation program with the World Bank, collaborating with Laos on a trilateral cooperation program, and the delivery of a workshop on the core ASEAN agreements. Key government interlocutors have spoken highly of Australia’s responsiveness and capacity to support the delivery of key Timor-Leste priorities.
